title: Finding triage has no verdict for 'fixed in this epic'
description:
From the ticks pwp run, 2026-09-15.

ticfac finding offers exactly two verdicts: --promote-as <tick> or --discard. A finding that was REPAIRED inside the epic fits neither. There is no tick to promote it to, so the only way to unblock the run is --discard, which the tool defines as 'record that a person looked and said no' and which prints 'The same finding reported again proposes nothing new, whatever was decided here.'

That suppression is the problem. A later review that correctly re-reports the issue — because the fix was reverted, lost in a merge, or never actually landed — is treated as proposing nothing new, on the strength of a decision that meant the opposite.

This happened for real: finding 9b346da7 (ci.yml naming a deleted package) was fixed on epic/pwp as commit 338bbf8b and then discarded, because discard was the only verdict that would let the run continue. The true meaning was recorded only in a tracker note, which is prose a future run is not obliged to read.

Add a third verdict, something like --fixed-as <sha>, that:
- unblocks the tick the way promote and discard do,
- records the commit that repaired it, so the claim is checkable rather than asserted,
- does NOT suppress a later report of the same finding: if it comes back, the fix did not hold, and that is exactly when the run must hear it.
notes: 2026-09-16 12:30 - ticfac run epic-9pd: attempt 11 merged into epic/9pd as 96bbe9b48947; the integrated gate (go) passed.
acceptance_criteria: A finding repaired inside the epic can be triaged as fixed, naming the commit; the run continues; and a later report of the same finding is NOT suppressed, proven by a test that re-reports it and asserts the run surfaces it again
